== Course of events ==

Having traveled with Dorothy through various perils, the Cowardly Lion is honored by the beasts, who bow to him and accept him as their King. The Cowardly Lion accepts this role, but he makes clear to the assembled beasts that his rule cannot begin at once: he promises that he will return and take up his place as King only once Dorothy is safely on her way to Kansas. This condition ties his new authority among the beasts directly to his loyalty toward Dorothy, whose journey home remains unfinished at this point.

The promise establishes an understanding between the Cowardly Lion and the beasts, who accept that his kingship is confirmed but that its exercise is deferred. Dorothy, Kansas, and the King are thus bound together in this moment: the beasts' recognition of the Cowardly Lion as King is conditional on Dorothy's eventual safe return to Kansas, and it is this promise that the Cowardly Lion carries forward as he continues traveling alongside Dorothy and her companions.
